Error Handling

When a request fails inside Cognee itself — permission denied, exhausted token budget, unmet prerequisites, missing dataset — the response carries that error's own HTTP status code and a single detail field holding the error message followed by the error class name:

{
  "detail": " []"
}

Routes still fall back to a generic body for unexpected, non-Cognee errors — 500 with {"error": "Internal server error", "detail": "..."} for search, and 409 with {"error": "..."} for recall, remember, and improve.

The remediation Hint

When Cognee knows what you would have to change to make the error go away, the detail-shaped body carries one extra key next to it:

{
  "detail": "LLM API key is not set. [LLMAPIKeyNotSetError]",
  "remediation": "Set LLM_API_KEY in your .env (copy .env.template to start). Cognee defaults to the OpenAI provider; set LLM_PROVIDER and LLM_MODEL as well to use another provider, and configure EMBEDDING_* too or embeddings fall back to OpenAI."
}

remediation is a short prescriptive hint naming the environment variable, flag, or install step to change — not a restatement of detail. It is optional and additive: the key is simply absent when no fix is known, so a client that reads only detail behaves exactly as before. Do not branch on its presence; treat it as a hint to show a human or an agent.

The hint comes from one of two places. Some errors carry their own (an unset LLM_API_KEY, a missing aws extra behind an s3:// path, an unsupported DB_PROVIDER). Everything else is matched against a shared table of common first-run failures: an API key rejected by the provider, an unset API key, a quota or billing denial, an unreachable EMBEDDING_ENDPOINT, an --ontology-file path that does not exist, and inconsistent LLM/embedding provider settings.

The generic {"error": ..., "detail": ...} fallback bodies described above are written by the routes themselves and never carry a remediation key.


  The same hint reaches transports that have no JSON body, because stringifying a Cognee error appends it: str(exc) ends with  Fix: . That is what the [CLI prints under a failed command and what the MCP server appends to tool error text. Each surface shows the hint once — an error that already carries a Fix: is not annotated again.


All API endpoints return standard HTTP status codes. Use the troubleshooting notes below when a request does not behave as expected.


  
    A 400 Bad Request usually means the request shape is invalid.

    Check the following:

    Malformed JSON: Make sure the request body is valid JSON and that quotes, commas, and braces are correct.
    Wrong content type: JSON requests should include Content-Type: application/json.
    Missing required fields: Compare your payload with the endpoint schema in the generated API reference below. In particular, POST /api/v1/recall and POST /api/v1/search require a query string — a body that omits it is rejected with 400 instead of being answered against a default question. Earlier releases declared a default of "What is in the document?" on that field, so a {} body returned 200; the placeholder is now only a schema example, and callers must send their own query.
    Wrong parameter names: Confirm field names such as query, datasets, or search_type exactly match the documented request body.
    External $ref in a graph_model schema: A custom graph schema may only point at its own document. A $ref that does not start with # — a URL, a file:// URI, or a filesystem path — is rejected instead of being fetched, so the server never makes a network request or reads a file on your behalf. On POST /api/v1/cognify this is a typed Cognee error, and the run never starts:

      {
        "detail": "graph_model contains an external $ref ('http://example.com/node.json'). Only in-document references starting with '#' are allowed; URLs and file paths are not fetched. ExternalSchemaReferenceError]"
      }

      POST /api/v1/remember reports the same rejection through its existing graph_model validation, which wraps the explanation rather than returning it verbatim. Its detail reads graph_model could not be converted to a graph model schema: ExternalSchemaReferenceError:  (Status code: 400). Expected the same dict format as the cognify endpoint, including a top-level 'title' key., so the error name arrives as a prefix instead of the [ExternalSchemaReferenceError] suffix shown above. The status is 400 on both routes — branch on the status, not on the body text. To fix it, inline each referenced schema into the document (typically under $defs) and point the $ref at it, for example #/$defs/Node.
  

  
    A 401 Unauthorized error means the server did not accept your authentication credentials.

    Check the following:

    Wrong auth method: Cognee Cloud uses X-Api-Key: YOUR-API-KEY. Self-hosted instances use Authorization: Bearer  after POST /api/v1/auth/login when authentication is enabled.
    Missing or expired token: If you are running locally with authentication enabled, register a user, log in again, and retry with a fresh Bearer token.
    Testing GET /api/v1/users/me without auth: This endpoint is mainly useful when you are explicitly testing authentication. For unauthenticated local development, use other endpoints instead.
    Backend access control enabled: If ENABLE_BACKEND_ACCESS_CONTROL=true, authentication is still required even when REQUIRE_AUTHENTICATION=false.

    For local auth setup, see [Deploy REST API Server.
  

  
    A 402 Payment Required means the token budget for the request is exhausted — on either the LLM or the embedding path, both of which classify it with the same detector. The provider (or the LiteLLM proxy enforcing a per-key/per-user spend cap) signalled that no budget remains. Search, recall, remember, and improve surface it with this body:

    {
      "detail": "LLM provider requires payment or token budget is exhausted. LLMPaymentRequiredError]"
    }

    When the provider's own budget sentence can be identified, it is included instead of the generic wording, with identifiers masked:

    {
      "detail": "LLM budget exhausted: Budget has been exceeded! Team= Current cost: 70.004, Max budget: 70.0 [LLMPaymentRequiredError]"
    }

    Spend and budget figures and the model name are kept — they are yours and they are the actionable part — while identifiers written as Virtual Key:, End User:, User=, Team=, Project=, Organization=, Tag=, or key_alias: are replaced with `. One form is currently not masked: the Key= (sk-…-hint) segment LiteLLM writes into Budget has been exceeded!`, which reaches the response body as the proxy sent it — a key alias and LiteLLM's own truncated key hint, not a usable credential.

    POST /api/v1/cognify and the LLM endpoints still return the legacy body {"error": "Token budget exhausted", "detail": "..."} — see [Knowledge Processing.

    This status is terminal — do the following:

    Do not retry: The request is excluded from automatic retries and re-submitting it will fail the same way until budget is restored.
    Top up the budget: Add token credits (or raise the spend cap) for the LLM provider or LiteLLM proxy, then re-run the request.
    Distinguish from 429: A 429 is transient throttling to back off on, while a 402 requires a budget change before the request can succeed. A LiteLLM-proxy spend-cap rejection reports as 429 at the proxy but is reclassified to 402 before it reaches you. For how that is detected, see Retry Behavior.
  

  
    A 403 Forbidden means you are authenticated but lack the required permission on the datasets the request touches. Cognee returns it with the standard error body:

    {
      "detail": "Request owner does not have permission: read] for any dataset. [PermissionDeniedError]"
    }

    The bracketed permission type reflects the operation — read for search and recall, write for remember and improve. A second variant, Request owner does not have necessary permission: [read] for all datasets requested., means at least one dataset you named is not accessible.

    Check the following:

    Dataset ownership: Confirm the dataset exists under your user or tenant, and that it was shared with you if it belongs to someone else.
    Named datasets: When you pass datasets or dataset_ids, every entry must be accessible — one inaccessible entry fails the whole request.
    Not a prerequisites problem: POST /api/v1/recall has always returned 403 for permission failures, but earlier releases dressed it in a misleading {"error": "Recall prerequisites not met", "hint": "..."} body suggesting you ingest and cognify first. The 403 now carries the real permission message. (Earlier versions of these docs described recall permission failures as a 200 with an empty list; that behavior never shipped.)
  

  
    A 404 Not Found usually means the route or resource does not exist.

    Check the following:

    Wrong path prefix: Use /api/v1/..., not /api/.... For example, /api/users/me returns a 404, while /api/v1/users/me is the correct path.
    Wrong HTTP method: Confirm you are using the method documented for the endpoint, such as POST for /api/v1/search.
    Missing resource: Dataset IDs, user IDs, or other resource identifiers may be validly formatted but not present in the current environment.
  

  
    A 409 with AmbiguousDataIdError in the detail field means you looked up a data item by id without naming a dataset, and that id matches documents in several datasets. This only happens to ids issued before the Cognee 1.5.0 [dataset-scoping upgrade: a record that was shared by several datasets was split into one document per dataset, and each split document still answers to the pre-split id.

    The error message lists every candidate as (dataset, data_id) pairs. Either repeat the call with a dataset_id to pick one, or use the candidate list to migrate your stored id mapping to the per-dataset ids once. An id with a single surviving match resolves directly and never triggers this error.

    (Recall, remember, and improve also return a generic 409 fallback body for unexpected errors — see above.)
  

  
    A 413 Request Entity Too Large means the add would push you past your stored-data or document-count limit. Cognee Cloud caps each member at 1 GB and 50,000 documents per workspace, checked by POST /api/v1/add (and POST /api/v1/add_text) before anything is stored:

    {"detail": "Storage quota exceeded. Used: 1073500000 bytes, incoming: 2000000 bytes, limit: 1074000000 bytes."}

    {"detail": "Document count quota exceeded. Current: 49998, incoming: 5, limit: 50000."}

    Do the following:

    Treat it as terminal: The whole call is rejected and none of its files are stored, so retrying it unchanged fails the same way.
    Check your usage: GET /api/v1/quotas/usage reports storageUsedInBytes against storageLimitInBytes.
    Free space or split the payload: Delete data you no longer need, or send fewer files per call if the incoming payload alone is what crosses the limit.

    POST /api/v1/remember is not subject to these limits. See Storage and document limits.
  

  
    A 429 Too Many Requests response means you have hit a rate limit.

    Try the following:

    Retry with backoff: Wait briefly before retrying, and increase the delay if the limit persists.
    Reduce burst traffic: Spread out large batches of requests instead of sending them all at once.
    Handle retries in code: Add retry logic so temporary throttling does not break your application flow.
  

  
    A 500 Internal Server Error usually indicates a server-side failure.

    Check the following:

    Server logs: Inspect the API server logs first to find the underlying exception.
    Provider configuration: Verify your LLM, graph database, and vector database settings are valid.
    Problem isolation: Retry with a smaller input or a simpler request to determine whether the issue is data-specific.
    Authentication and permissions side effects: If the error appears only in multi-user mode, verify your auth and permissions configuration.
  



  Always implement proper error handling in your applications to gracefully handle API failures and rate limits.

Memify
Source: https://docs.cognee.ai/api-reference/memify/memify

/cognee_openapi_spec.json post /api/v1/memify
Enrichment pipeline in Cognee, can work with already built graphs. If no data is provided existing knowledge graph will be used as data,

Provided tasks and data will be arranged to run the Cognee pipeline and execute graph enrichment/creation.

      Unknown names are rejected with 422. Tasks requiring parameters are SDK-only.
enrichmentTasks Optional[List[str]]: Names of built-in Cognee Tasks to handle enrichment of provided graph/data from extraction tasks.
      Supported names: cognify_session, cognify_agent_trace_feedback, apply_feedback_weights,
      merge_entity_duplicates, index_data_points.
data Optional[List[str]]: The data to ingest. Can be any text data when custom extraction and enrichment tasks are used.
      Data provided here will be forwarded to the first extraction task in the pipeline as input.
      If no data is provided the whole graph (or subgraph if node_name/node_type is specified) will be forwarded
dataset_name (Optional[str]): Name of the datasets to memify
dataset_id (Optional[UUID]): List of UUIDs of an already existing dataset
node_name (Optional[List[str]]):  Filter graph to specific named entities (for targeted search). Used when no data is provided.
run_in_background (Optional[bool]): Whether to execute processing asynchronously. Defaults to False (blocking).

Either datasetName or datasetId must be provided.

Response
Returns information about the add operation containing:
Status of the operation
Details about the processed data
Any relevant metadata from the ingestion process

403 Forbidden: User doesn't have permission to use dataset
422 Unprocessable Content: Unknown task name in extractionTasks/enrichmentTasks

datasetId value can only be the UUID of an already existing dataset

Recall: query memory with auto-routed search type and session-first lookup
Source: https://docs.cognee.ai/api-reference/recall/recall:-query-memory-with-auto-routed-search-type-and-session-first-lookup

/cognee_openapi_spec.json post /api/v1/recall
Recall information from the knowledge graph.

This is a memory-oriented alias for the search endpoint. All search
types and options from v1 are supported.

Request Parameters
Field names are shown camelCased in the schema (e.g. searchType, datasetIds,
topK); both camelCase and snake_case are accepted.

search_type (Optional[SearchType]): Type of search to perform. Omit
  (default: null) to auto-route the query with the rule-based router
  (HYBRID_COMPLETION fallback); pass a value to pin one.
datasets (Optional[List[str]]): Dataset names to search within
dataset_ids (Optional[List[UUID]]): Dataset UUIDs to search within;
  take precedence over dataset names when both are provided
query (str): The search query string
system_prompt (Optional[str]): System prompt for completion searches
node_name (Optional[List[str]]): Filter to specific node sets
top_k (Optional[int]): Maximum results (default: 15)
only_context (bool): Return what the LLM would have received instead of
  its answer — for completion types each item's text is the user prompt
  (conversation history, question plus retrieval context, session guidance)
  and its system_prompt field the retriever's task template; retrieval-only
  types return their context
verbose (bool): Verbose output
include_references (bool): Include source/provenance references in
  completion results (default: true)
stream (Optional[bool]): Stream the answer as server-sent events
  (text/event-stream). Defaults to content negotiation on Accept.
session_id (Optional[str]): Session whose cached QA and trace entries
  should be searched
scope (Optional[str | List[str]]): Memory sources to include: "graph",
  "session", "session_first", "trace", "session_context", "tools", "code",
  "all", "auto", or a list of these (default: "auto" — session first when
  session_id is set, else graph). "session_first" requests that short-circuit
  explicitly rather than by omitting searchType. "code" is explicit opt-in only
  and returns deterministic code-graph facts tagged source="code"
  (e.g. scope=["graph", "code"])
code_query (Optional[dict]): "code" scope only — operation and arguments
  for the code-graph query (same format as /v1/search code_query); omit for
  the default "explore" with the query text as seed
response_schema (Optional[dict]): JSON Schema for structured
  completion output; validated results land in each result's
  `structured` field. 422 on schemas outside the supported subset.
contextProfile (str): Profile to render for the 'session_context' scope: 'qa'
  (conversational) or 'agent' (tool/workflow). Ignored by other scopes. Defaults to 'qa'.
toolConnections (Optional[List[str]]): Names of authorized external database
  connections for the 'tools' scope. Omit to use every connection visible to the caller.
toolsTrigger (str): When the 'tools' scope runs: 'always', or 'on_empty' to query the
  external database only when every other requested source returned nothing. Defaults to
  'always'.

Error Codes
402/403/404/409/422: Cognee errors (payment required, permission
  denied, missing user, session-dataset conflict, prerequisites not met) return their own
  status code and message via the global error handler
409 Conflict: Unexpected non-Cognee error during recall

session_id (Optional[str]): Required for qa/trace/feedback entries; optional for
  skill_run entries.
skill_improvement (Optional[dict]): Skill improvement details forwarded to
  remember when recording a skill run.

Response
The returned `RememberResult includes entry_type` and
`entry_id — the qa_id/trace_id` returned by the cache
(or the `qa_id` a feedback was attached to). Use this to chain
feedback to a freshly stored QA.

Remember: ingest data and build the knowledge graph (add + cognify + improve)
Source: https://docs.cognee.ai/api-reference/remember/remember:-ingest-data-and-build-the-knowledge-graph-add-+-cognify-+-improve

/cognee_openapi_spec.json post /api/v1/remember
Ingest data and build the knowledge graph in a single call.

This endpoint combines the add and cognify steps. Data is ingested
first, then automatically processed into a structured knowledge graph.

Request Parameters
data (List[UploadFile]): Files to upload and process.
raw_data (Optional[List[str]]): String inputs, one entry each: raw text, a
  local file or directory path on the server (requires ACCEPT_LOCAL_FILE_PATH), a
  web URL fetched as a page (requires ALLOW_HTTP_REQUESTS), or a GitHub/GitLab
  repository URL, shallow-cloned and indexed as a code graph. Uploads come first,
  then raw_data entries; labels and external_metadata pair with that combined
  order. Normal ingestion only — rejected with content_type. At least one of data
  or raw_data is required for normal ingestion.
labels (Optional[str]): JSON array of per-file labels, e.g.
  ["finance", "people", ""], paired positionally with the uploaded files (one
  entry per file; an empty entry skips that file). Stored on each file's data
  record. Normal ingestion only — rejected with session_id or content_type.
external_metadata (Optional[str]): JSON array of per-file metadata objects,
  e.g. [\{"source": "crm"\}, null], paired positionally with the uploaded files
  (one entry per file; null or \{\} skips that file). Merged into each file's
  stored external_metadata. Normal ingestion only — rejected with session_id
  or content_type.
datasetName (Optional[str]): Name of the target dataset.
datasetId (Optional[UUID]): UUID of an existing dataset.
session_id (Optional[str]): Session to attribute this memory to. When set,
  data is stored in the session cache and bridged into the permanent graph in the
  background; the session is tracked in the sessions dashboard. When omitted,
  data is ingested directly via add + cognify.
node_set (Optional[List[str]]): Node identifiers for graph organisation.
run_in_background (Optional[bool]): Run the cognify step asynchronously (default: False).
self_improvement (Optional[bool]): Run the improve loop after cognify
  (default: True). False gives a plain add + cognify ingestion.
custom_prompt (Optional[str]): Custom prompt for entity extraction.
chunk_size (Optional[int]): Maximum tokens per chunk (default: 4096).
chunks_per_batch (Optional[int]): Chunks per cognify batch.
ontology_key (Optional[List[str]]): Reference to one or more previously uploaded ontology files to use for knowledge graph construction.
graph_model (Optional[str]): JSON-serialised graph model schema (same dict format accepted by the cognify endpoint).
content_type (Optional[str]): Set to "skills" to ingest SKILL.md files as
  Skill nodes, or "code" to index whole repositories — each raw_data entry is
  then a git URL or server-local repo path and one code graph is built per
  entry (poll progress via GET /v1/datasets/status?pipeline=code_graph_pipeline);
  omit for normal ingestion.
index_vectors (Optional[bool]): content_type="code" only — also embed the
  extracted code facts for semantic retrievers (default false, no LLM/embedding
  calls otherwise).

Either datasetName or datasetId must be provided.
import_mode (Optional[str]): COGX archive imports only: 'preserve' (default),
  'hybrid', or 're-derive'.
skill_name (Optional[str]): content_type='skills' + skills_text only: name/slug for
  the inline skill (defaults to 'skill').
skills_text (Optional[str]): content_type='skills' only: inline SKILL.md markdown to
  ingest without a file upload (no-code path). When set and no files are uploaded, it is
  written to a temporary SKILL.md and ingested via the normal skills pipeline. Pair with
  skill_name to control the resulting skill name.

Error Codes
400 Bad Request: Neither datasetId nor datasetName provided, unsupported
  content_type, invalid graph_model JSON/schema, or invalid code-ingestion
  combination (no raw_data repository specs, file uploads or session_id with
  content_type="code", index_vectors without it, or local repo paths while
  ACCEPT_LOCAL_FILE_PATH=false)
409 Conflict: Error during processing

Sync To Cloud
Source: https://docs.cognee.ai/api-reference/sync/sync-to-cloud

/cognee_openapi_spec.json post /api/v1/sync
Sync local data to Cognee Cloud.

This endpoint triggers synchronization of local Cognee data to your cloud instance.
It uploads your local datasets, knowledge graphs, and processed data to the cloud
for backup, sharing, or cloud-based processing.

Request Body (JSON)
{
    "dataset_ids": ["123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000", "456e7890-e12b-34c5-d678-901234567000"]
}

Response
Returns immediate response for the sync operation:
run_id: Unique identifier for tracking the background sync operation
status: Always "started" (operation runs in background)
dataset_ids: List of dataset IDs being synced
dataset_names: List of dataset names being synced
message: Description of the background operation
timestamp: When the sync was initiated
user_id: User who initiated the sync

Cloud Sync Features
Automatic Authentication: Uses your Cognee Cloud credentials
Data Compression: Optimizes transfer size for faster uploads
Smart Sync: Automatically handles data updates efficiently
Progress Tracking: Monitor sync status with sync_id
Error Recovery: Automatic retry for failed transfers
Data Validation: Ensures data integrity during transfer

Example Usage
Sync multiple datasets to cloud by IDs (JSON request)
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/api/v1/sync" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Cookie: auth_token=your-token" \
  -d '{"dataset_ids": ["123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000", "456e7890-e12b-34c5-d678-901234567000"]}'

Sync all user datasets (empty request body or null dataset_ids)
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/api/v1/sync" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Cookie: auth_token=your-token" \
  -d '{}'

Error Codes
400 Bad Request: Invalid dataset_ids format
401 Unauthorized: Invalid or missing authentication
403 Forbidden: User doesn't have permission to access dataset
404 Not Found: Dataset not found
409 Conflict: Sync operation conflict or cloud service unavailable
413 Payload Too Large: Dataset too large for current cloud plan
429 Too Many Requests: Rate limit exceeded

Notes
Sync operations run in the background - you get an immediate response
Use the returned run_id to track progress (status API coming soon)
Large datasets are automatically chunked for efficient transfer
Cloud storage usage counts against your plan limits
The sync will continue even if you close your connection

Update
Source: https://docs.cognee.ai/api-reference/update/update

/cognee_openapi_spec.json patch /api/v1/update
Update data in a dataset.

This endpoint updates existing documents in a specified dataset by providing the data_id of the existing document
to update and the new document with the changes as the data.
The document is updated, analyzed, and the changes are integrated into the knowledge graph.

Request Parameters
data_id (UUID, required, query): UUID of the existing document to update (returned by GET /api/v1/datasets/\{dataset_id\}/data)
dataset_id (UUID, required, query): UUID of the dataset containing the document to update
data (List[UploadFile]): New version of the document that replaces the existing one.
node_set (Optional[List[str]]): List of node identifiers for graph organization and access control.
         Used for grouping related data points in the knowledge graph.
chunk_level_diff (bool, query, default true): Replace only the chunks affected
         by the edit instead of re-ingesting the whole document.

Response
One body on every path (UpdateResult), a superset of the chunk-level summary
returned before:
status: "incremental" (chunks replaced), "unchanged" (no content change),
  "full_rebuild" (memory dropped and rebuilt from the new content) or "failed" (the rebuild's
  cognify run errored; error says why, and the call can be retried).
regions, deleted_chunks, added_chunks, reused_chunks,
  kept_chunks, reindexed_chunks, total_chunks: the chunk-level
  counters; null on a rebuild, which has no diff.
data_id, dataset_id: the document, the handle to retry with.
duration_seconds: wall-clock time of the update.
pipeline_run_id: the run to inspect; null for a no-op.
fallback: set on every rebuild; its reason names why the chunk-level path
  did not run (disabled, unsupported_metadata, custom_extraction_config,
  per_call_db_config, unsupported_backend, unsupported_chunker,
  no_baseline, chunks_not_tiling, unreadable_text) and detail says it in
  a sentence.
error: error_class and message when status is "failed".

Error Codes
422 Unprocessable Entity: data_id or dataset_id missing or not a valid UUID
403 Forbidden: User lacks write permission on the dataset
404 Not Found: data_id resolves to no document in the dataset
500 Internal Server Error: the rebuild's cognify run errored (body is the
  UpdateResult with status "failed") or an unexpected error occurred

Notes
Chunk-level updates keep unaffected chunks, their entities, and their summaries
  untouched; only the edited region is re-extracted.

Changelog
Source: https://docs.cognee.ai/changelog

Recent Cognee releases

Cognee releases with highlights and links to the full release notes on GitHub.

Unreleased

Changes queued for the next release. This section is updated as unreleased work is merged and is folded into a versioned release section when the release is published.

Highlights

Requires HTTP 403 rather than 409 when a user probes another user's dataset status, completing the permission-denial contract started in v1.6.0. A permission denial is now documented separately from an unexpected conflict, and the remediation hint attached to it is scoped to LiteLLM so a dataset ACL error no longer suggests changing LLM billing (SDK-635, PR #5132).
Includes the bundled Ladybug extension binaries in the source distribution, not only the wheel. The binaries are gitignored and injected at build time, so uv build's sdist-first flow produced a wheel without them — a wheel built from the sdist fell back to downloading the JSON extension from extension.ladybugdb.com, the dependency v1.6.0 removed. Wheel packaging is unchanged (PR #5138).

v1.6.0

Released: September 18, 2026\
[View on GitHub

The first release since v1.5.4, carrying 59 merged pull requests. Its theme is making an install with no LLM key at all a working setup: the LLM-free extractor and the local embedder now resolve by default rather than by hand, and the packages they need moved out of optional extras into the core dependency list, so a bare pip install cognee can ingest and answer. Alongside that, pipeline startup recovery stops deleting completed work, update() returns one result shape on every path, completion searches no longer answer from an empty graph with the LLM's deflection, and two credential defaults that shipped as publicly known strings are gone.

Highlights

Makes only_context=True return the full LLM input on completion search types, and removes the context_format parameter that shipped in 1.5.4 to make that opt-in. only_context promised "what the LLM would have received" but handed back the bare retrieval context, while a real completion is also sent the conversation history, the question and context rendered through the retriever's templates, and the session guidance block. The opt-in knob closed that gap only for callers who knew to ask and changed the return type when they did, so the layers are now always included. For completion types the result is the user prompt; the system prompt — the retriever's task template — travels beside it, because the LLM receives the two as separate messages: on recall() they are item.text and item.system_prompt, and on search(verbose=True) they are user_prompt_result and system_prompt_result, now always present rather than gated on a requested format. Both are assembled by the same build_session_prompt (read-only) and build_completion_prompts the real completion uses, so preview and production cannot drift, and the call makes no LLM completion or turn-analysis call, writes nothing back to the session, and records no QA turn. It is not free: the session layer's conversation-history recall embeds the query, one embedding call made once per search and shared across a multi-dataset fan-out, and only when a prompt is actually built. Retrieval-only types (CHUNKS, SUMMARIES, CODE, …) have no template and CYPHER and AGENTIC_COMPLETION opt out, so they still return their bare context with no system prompt; an empty retrieval also falls back to the bare context, so "nothing found" stays detectable. recall() returns a single item for the prompt rather than one per context entry, since the prompt is one artifact. Migrating: passing context_format= to search() or recall() now raises TypeError, and contextFormat on POST /api/v1/search and POST /api/v1/recall is ignored rather than rejected; the "prompt" envelope dict and its session_context_result key are gone — read the two prompt fields directly. The preview stays knowingly unfaithful in one place: a real sequential turn first rewrites the question with an LLM call this path must not make, so the raw query fills the question slot, selects the history, and ranks the guidance block (PR #5085).
Stops completion searches answering from an empty graph with the LLM's polite deflection. On a fresh install, before cognify, or after memory was dropped, a completion search sent the empty context to the LLM anyway and returned "There is no context provided…" as a normal, non-empty result — so a caller checking if results: could not distinguish "no memory found" from a real answer. The two emptinesses now behave differently: an empty graph raises a typed 404 rather than inventing a run, and an empty retrieval context on a populated graph skips the LLM call entirely and reports a typed status instead of a fabricated sentence. HYBRID retrieval raises NoDataError on an empty graph for the same reason. The query router behind recall() was simplified alongside this and now falls back to HYBRID when a routed search type fails, rather than surfacing the routing failure (fixes #3728; SDK-270, SDK-545, PRs #5052, #5084, #4889).
Makes search() and recall() fail on a dataset name that resolves to nothing, instead of silently narrowing the scope. Names are resolved through a membership filter in get_dataset_ids, so a name matching no dataset simply dropped out: search(datasets="real", "typo"]) answered from real alone with nothing in the response saying typo was never searched — while the same request expressed as UUIDs had always failed outright. get_dataset_ids and get_authorized_existing_datasets take a strict: bool = False flag, and the search and recall paths pass strict=True, so an unresolvable name now fails the whole request with a typed error naming it. Requests that list only resolvable names are unchanged (SDK-747, PR #5109).
Makes an install with no LLM key at all a working setup instead of a first-call failure, and renames the open-source GLiNER extractor to gliner_demo. Cognee already shipped both an LLM-free extractor and a local embedder, but each had to be selected by hand, so a fresh keyless install died at the first extraction call. [GRAPH_EXTRACTOR now defaults to auto, which resolves per run — the LLM path when a usable LLM key is configured, the GLiNER demo model when none is — and untouched embedding settings resolve to fastembed with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (384 dimensions, read from the fastembed registry) whenever there is no key to reuse for the OpenAI default. The two halves resolve independently: any credential, any explicit EMBEDDING_* value, or a GRAPH_EXTRACTOR of llm takes its half back to the configured provider, and values in a .env file count as configured — so configured deployments are unchanged. The variables that skip the provider preflight (COGNEE_SKIP_PREFLIGHT, COGNEE_SKIP_CONNECTION_TEST, MOCK_EMBEDDING) also switch the rerouting off, since a mocked or deliberately partial config should be honoured rather than replaced. With no key and gliner2 missing, cognify() now fails up front with KeylessExtractorNotInstalledError and the install command (pip install "cogneegliner]") rather than mid-run. Alongside that, the extractor is named the way the Postgres demo backend is: gliner_demo everywhere ([extractor="gliner_demo", GRAPH_EXTRACTOR=gliner_demo, cognee.tasks.graph.gliner_demo), with gliner kept as an alias so existing settings and calls keep working, and selecting it logs one notice per process saying the open-source extractor is a demo of cognee's enterprise GLiNER extraction. Recall Without an LLM Key runs the whole keyless round trip, down to recall() answering with CHUNKS when no LLM can write a completion (SDK-691, PR #5086; COG-6588, PR #5095).
Moves fastembed, onnxruntime and enola-cli out of optional extras and into the core dependency list, so the keyless defaults above work on a bare pip install cognee with nothing extra selected. Keyless ingestion needs a local embedder, and fastembed is cheap enough to always ship: onnxruntime plus a 1 MB package, about 65 MB, against the 415 MB–2 GB torch stack the gliner extra carries — so a bare install can now embed and answer CHUNKS recalls with no key set, and the keyless install hint shrinks to one extra, cogneegliner]. enola-cli moves the same way, pinned at ==0.4.21, because it powers the built-in deterministic code-graph route; the pin is deliberate (its snapshot contract and known answers are validated by test_code_graph_e2e.py) and [tool.uv] exclude-newer-package lets a newly pinned release resolve inside the repository's two-day exclude-newer window. 0.4.21 is also the first release with musllinux_1_2 wheels for both architectures, verified on Alpine 3.24 ARM64 and x86\_64, so Alpine installs work where 0.4.20 had no compatible wheel. cognee[fastembed] and cognee[codegraph] are now empty extras, kept only so existing install commands stay valid — both resolve to nothing and neither is needed any more. onnxruntime is constrained per interpreter (=1.24.1 on 3.14, which is the first version with cp314 wheels). Upgrade action: none required, but expect a larger baseline install; drop [fastembed] and [codegraph] from install commands and Dockerfiles at your convenience. pydantic-settings also gains a floor, >=2.2.1 → >=2.7.0, for the NoDecode annotation used by cognee/modules/improve/config.py (SDK-562, PRs #5092, #5123).
Rounds out the keyless path with the fixes found running it from a clean environment. A first keyless remember() or cognify() downloads the GLiNER demo model (fastino/gliner2.5-base-v1, about 750 MB) and the fastembed embedder (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, about 65 MB) through the Hugging Face hub; the only trace was a tqdm progress bar on stderr, invisible outside a terminal and silent about what was being fetched, so a first call that took minutes looked like a hang. Cognee now announces each download before it starts, naming the model and its size. Alongside it: add() no longer probes the LLM at all — it stages data and makes no LLM call of its own, the three media loaders are the only ingestion step that does and they now raise a clear LLMAPIKeyNotSetError at the point of use, so the add-time probe was a duplicate of a decision remember() already makes from its real task list; file uploads that use GLiNER no longer report a spurious missing-LLM-key error; the improve() session bridge runs without a key; the code route stays off the keyless extractor gate; and session trace-context extraction is skipped when there is no key rather than failing noisily. Stages that genuinely need an LLM now skip cleanly instead of failing partway (SDK-738, SDK-748, SDK-753, SDK-754, PRs #5094, #5108, #5114, #5118, #5119).
Rejects external $ref values in a client-supplied [graph_model schema instead of resolving them server-side. A graph_model sent to POST /api/v1/cognify — or to POST /api/v1/remember, which shares the same converter — went straight into datamodel-code-generator, which resolves $ref natively: a $ref to an https:// URL was fetched by the server and used to build the model, and a $ref to a local path was read off the server's disk, with the file's contents landing in the JSON schema handed to the LLM. The converter now walks the schema before generating anything and raises ExternalSchemaReferenceError (400) for any $ref that does not start with # — at any depth, including refs nested inside anyOf — and GenerateConfig(allow_remote_refs=False) is set as a second layer, so no network request is made and no file is read while references are resolved. In-document pointers are unaffected: #/$defs/Node is what Pydantic emits for nested models, so a schema produced by graph_model_to_graph_schema() or by the UI graph-model editor keeps working unchanged. The cognify route also re-raises CogneeApiError before its catch-all, so the rejection renders as {"detail": "graph_model contains an external $ref (...). Only in-document references starting with '#' are allowed; URLs and file paths are not fetched. ExternalSchemaReferenceError]"} rather than a 500 echoing the exception text; remember wraps the same explanation in its existing graph_model could not be converted to a graph model schema: ... body, so branch on the 400 status rather than on the body text. If you referenced a schema by URL or path, inline it (typically under $defs) and point the $ref at the inlined copy. No public API signature, configuration option, environment variable, or migration ships with the fix (SDK-719, PR #5073).
Changes the [shipped default LLM from openai/gpt-5-mini to openai/gpt-5.6-luna, OpenAI's low-cost gpt-5.6 tier. The swap covers the default everywhere it is user-facing: llm_model, the BAML backend's baml_llm_model (now gpt-5.6-luna), the unprefixed gpt-5.6-luna that cognee config unset llm_model resets to on the CLI, the shipped .env.example, the commented LLM_MODEL / LLM_SUMMARIZATION_MODEL / LLM_QUERY_MODEL / BAML_LLM_MODEL lines in .env.template, the starter kit's own .env.template, and the Docker sandbox kit, which now pins LLM_MODEL=openai/gpt-5.6-luna. The Settings UI's OpenAI model list offers gpt-5.6-luna first, with gpt-5-mini retained below it, so switching back is a dropdown choice rather than a hand-typed id. Local session cost estimates gain the whole gpt-5.6 series — luna, terra, sol, and astra — so the new default's spend is priced rather than falling through to the unknown-model $0; at $0.20/$1.20 per 1M input/output tokens against gpt-5-mini's $0.25/$2.00, it is cheaper on input and 40% cheaper on output, so estimates for an unpinned deployment will drift down. Behavior is otherwise unchanged: gpt-5.6-luna still matches the gpt-5 checks that select json_schema_mode on the instructor path and that mark a model as a reasoning model for token budgeting, and it inherits the same provider-side restriction on LLM_TEMPERATURE, which should stay unset. Only deployments that never set LLM_MODEL are affected — an explicitly pinned model is untouched, and a value that merely happens to equal the default still counts as explicitly set. If you relied on the implicit old default, pin LLM_MODEL=openai/gpt-5-mini and audit env templates and CI. No API signature, new configuration option, environment variable, or migration ships with the change (PR #5046).
Bounds seed selection for the default graph visualization. A bare visualize_graph() call used to rank node degree by loading every node and edge into Python, which exhausted the worker on a 5.59M-node / 35.64M-edge graph before it could pick ten ids. Seed selection now delegates to get_top_degree_node_ids(top_k) on the graph adapter: Ladybug, Neo4j, Neptune, Postgres, and Turso rank both endpoints of at most 200,000 sampled edges inside the store and return ids only (Postgres and Turso materialize one sample for both edge directions), and an id-only query tops up sparse samples so isolated nodes stay valid seeds. The ranking is approximate by contract — the sample is a physical prefix of the stored edges, not a random one, so seeds skew toward earlier-ingested data and recent hubs in a large graph can stay invisible; it bounds the aggregation and the returned data, not query-planning cost or latency. The method is declared on GraphDBInterface but is not abstract: an adapter that does not override it inherits the full-graph Python count and logs a memory-cost warning once per adapter type per process, so existing adapters keep working. All implementations reject top_k  record, relational store unavailable (...)), every other persistence failure keeps the existing warning with its traceback, and both write sites — the record_operation scope and the deferred close — get the same two-clause shape. Note the classification is by exception type, not by whether the failure was expected: a real outage that surfaces as an OperationalError — a refused Postgres connection, a connection timeout, a SQLite lock timeout — is now skipped just as quietly, so a ledger that has stopped recording shows up as missing rows rather than as warnings; set LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG to observe the skipped writes. Operator action: anyone alerting or grepping on record_operation: failed to persist lines will stop seeing them for the store-unavailable case. No public API signature, configuration option, environment variable, or migration ships with the fix, and the fail-open contract is unchanged — the write attempt is still the only probe, with no pre-check for the database's existence (SDK-399, PR #5081).
Removes the insecure literal default for the three authentication token secrets. FASTAPI_USERS_JWT_SECRET, FASTAPI_USERS_RESET_PASSWORD_TOKEN_SECRET, and FASTAPI_USERS_VERIFICATION_TOKEN_SECRET all fell back to the string super_secret when unset, a publicly known value that let anyone forge a valid token against a deployment that never configured them. Each variable now resolves through a shared helper: the configured value if it is set and non-blank (surrounding whitespace is stripped, so a blank value counts as unset), otherwise a random secret generated once per process per variable. This is a behavior change for deployments that never set these variables. The old default was constant, so tokens survived restarts and were accepted across replicas; a generated secret is known only to the process that made it, so every restart invalidates every token it issued and no two processes agree on one. Anything running more than one process — uvicorn workers, several replicas, or separate API and worker processes — must now set all three explicitly to the same securely generated values, and a single-process deployment must set them to keep logins, password reset links, and email verification links working across a restart. The API server reports this at boot: its lifespan resolves all three and logs a warning for each one it had to generate, naming the variable and what stops working without it, and stays silent when all three are set. Resolution itself never logs, so import cognee in SDK, CLI, and MCP usage — none of which verifies tokens — is unaffected. .env.template now ships all three commented out with the new behavior described, and the unused cognee/get_token.py token-minting helper, which carried its own super_secret fallback, is deleted. No public API signature, endpoint, configuration option, or migration ships with the fix (SDK-720, PR #5062).
Removes the known default-user password, which gave nearly every install a superuser with publicly documented credentials. create_default_user fell back to the literal string default_password when DEFAULT_USER_PASSWORD was unset, and because the account is created lazily from the SDK, CLI and API paths alike, any instance later served over the network with authentication enabled carried a known-credential admin login. The default user is now created with no password at all: hashed_password holds the "!" sentinel, the Unix locked-account convention, which is not a valid hash — so verify_and_update raises UnknownHashError and the existing error path rejects the login rather than comparing against anything. DEFAULT_USER_PASSWORD sets the password once, only when none exists, and never changes an existing one. Upgrade action: deployments that relied on the implicit default_password login must set DEFAULT_USER_PASSWORD before upgrading, or set a password on the account through the normal user-management path; existing explicitly-set passwords are untouched (SDK-549, PR #5016).
Adds a remediation hint to Cognee errors: a short prescriptive fix naming the environment variable, flag, or install step to change. Errors that know their own fix carry it (an unset LLM_API_KEY, a missing aws extra behind an s3:// path, an unsupported DB_PROVIDER); everything else is matched against a shared table of common first-run failures — a rejected or unset API key, a quota or billing denial, an unreachable EMBEDDING_ENDPOINT, a missing --ontology-file, inconsistent LLM/embedding provider settings. str(exc) on a CogneeApiError now ends with  Fix:  when one is set, the REST API returns it as an optional remediation key next to detail in CogneeApiError responses, the CLI prints it under the failed command, and the MCP server appends it to remember, recall, and forget error output. The key is additive: clients that read only detail are unaffected.
Publishes cognee-mcp to PyPI from CI through a dedicated release_mcp.yml workflow, replacing the hand uploads that left the package at 0.5.5 while the whole FastMCP 3 migration went unpublished. The MCP server versions independently of the library (0.5.x against 1.5.x), so it gets its own workflow and its own tag namespace, cognee-mcp-v, rather than riding the library release. The workflow is run by hand from main and refuses any other ref; before building it checks that the version in cognee-mcp/pyproject.toml is not already on PyPI and that the tag is free, so an immutable-version collision fails up front with a message naming the fix (bump the version and re-lock) instead of at the upload step. It verifies uv.lock matches pyproject.toml and that the locked cognee satisfies the declared range, builds on Python 3.12, and publishes over PyPI Trusted Publishing (OIDC) with PEP 740 attestations and a GitHub-hosted SLSA build-provenance attestation — the same posture as the library release — so gh attestation verify ./cognee_mcp--py3-none-any.whl --repo topoteretes/cognee works for MCP wheels. The tag is pushed only after the upload succeeds, and no GitHub release is created. For users this means uvx cognee-mcp@latest and uv pip install cognee-mcp now track releases; the Local Setup page points at the package as the default install path. 0.5.5 and earlier carry no attestations. Operators must register a third PyPI trusted publisher for the cognee-mcp project; the one on cognee does not cover it (SDK-620, PR #5021).
Gives the MCP server a memory-hit summary on recall and per-write ontology selection on remember. A recall result now opens with a line such as 2 memories found (2 from sessions) above the unchanged body, so a caller can see whether memory contributed at all; system status markers do not count as hits. An empty result is no longer ambiguous — dataset-scoped pipeline progress and graph summaries separate indexing in progress, empty graph, unindexed dataset, indexing failed and no match, with queued background ingestion recognised before its pipeline status is even recorded; the diagnostics carry a two-second timeout and report status as unavailable rather than guessing, and a successful hit skips them entirely. Separately, remember writes accept ontology_key="workspace_v2" or ontology_key="organizations", "software"] to select uploaded ontologies per write: API mode sends repeated ontology_key multipart fields, local mode resolves them through OntologyService and passes the resolver into the extraction configuration, and both foreground and background writes forward the selection. Session-only writes reject a nonempty ontology_key because they perform no extraction, and omitting the argument preserves the configured ontology (SDK-438, SDK-681, PRs #5060, #5063).
Expands the opt-in [entity consolidation memify pipeline from a single entity-description rewrite into three stages: each Entity description is rewritten from its graph neighborhood, each EntityType description is then summarized from its actual members (always stating the member count, naming members individually only at or below type_max_named_members, default 5), and every member's is_a edge gets edge_text of the form {Name} is a {Type}: ... so the type membership is searchable rather than a bare is_a label. Entity.is_a widens from EntityType to EntityType | tuple, where the tuple is (Edge(relationship_type="is_a", edge_text=...), EntityType), and an entity can carry more than one type. consolidate_entity_descriptions_pipeline() still takes no required arguments but now exposes per-call caps on LLM concurrency, prompt size, type batch size, the naming threshold, persisted is_a length, and completion-token budgets — see the guide's Tuning table for names and defaults. A failed entity rewrite keeps the existing description and a failed type summary is skipped, so one provider error no longer discards the whole run (SDK-435, PR #4613).
Fixes session turns being lost or mis-recorded when the session-context analysis decided they needed no answer. A feedback-only or instruction-only message ("that last answer was wrong", "keep answers short") is gated by the analysis and served a short acknowledgement instead of a generated answer — but neither session-search path handled that correctly. Sequential returned the acknowledgement before add_qa ever ran, so the user's message was dropped from history outright; concurrent recorded the turn but ignored the gate, storing and returning the answer its parallel lane had already generated and crediting it with the graph elements and guidance ids that answer had used. Either way the session could not act cleanly on an instruction it had just been given. Both paths now share one gate decision: a gated turn is appended as its own QA entry — raw message as question, acknowledgement as answer, empty context, and None for used_graph_element_ids / used_session_context_ids, since the acknowledgement came from neither retrieval nor session guidance and the next turn's analysis must not be handed guidance the user never saw. Three things change for consumers. cognee.session.get_session() now returns an entry per turn sequential mode used to drop, and in concurrent mode a gated entry's answer is the acknowledgement with its used_* fields cleared — so history grows slightly and the fixed 10-entry conversation window is partly consumed by acknowledgement turns; in concurrent mode a gated recall() / search() now returns the acknowledgement rather than generated text, with no retrieved objects, no context, and no Evidence: block under include_references=True — review anything that assumed every answer field holds a generated reply; and because session persistence ingests every QA entry without filtering, acknowledgement turns now reach the graph too when you run improve(session_ids=...]). For streaming recall the deltas of the discarded answer have already been emitted by the time the gate lands, so render the final payload over what was streamed rather than appending to it. No public API signature, configuration option, environment variable, or migration ships with the fix, and AUTO_FEEDBACK=false still removes turn gating altogether (SDK-402, PR #4580).
Fixes first-use [dataset database provisioning failing when two callers raced on a dataset whose backing databases did not exist yet. A recall()/search() arriving while the first ingestion was still running, or two simultaneous add() calls, could both pass the "does this dataset already have a database?" check and both try to insert the same DatasetDatabase registry row — the loser raised an IntegrityError, which surfaced over HTTP as a 500. The insert is now conflict-tolerant: the caller that loses re-reads the winner's row and carries on with it. That is safe because dataset_id is the registry's primary key and every handler derives its physical database and schema names from the dataset id, so both callers had provisioned the same backing databases; if no row exists after the failed insert the original error is still re-raised, so an unrelated integrity failure is not swallowed. This half of the fix is backend-agnostic and applies to every dataset database handler. Postgres needed a second half, because IF NOT EXISTS is not race-free there: two transactions that both pass the check still collide on the catalog's unique index, and CREATE DATABASE has no IF NOT EXISTS at all. Creators are now serialized on advisory locks in the cognee_provisioning namespace — a session-level pg_advisory_lock around the pg_database check plus CREATE DATABASE for the database-per-dataset handlers, and a transaction-scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock around CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector and CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS for the shared-database handlers. Expect brief blocking, not errors: a concurrent first-use caller now waits while the winner finishes its DDL, and because the schema lock is keyed on the shared database, first use of different datasets in that one database serializes too. Both locks release automatically — the session lock in a finally, or by Postgres itself if the connection drops — and pg_advisory_lock needs no special grant. Sequential callers see no change, subsequent accesses to an already-provisioned dataset are untouched, and no public API signature, configuration option, environment variable, or migration ships with the fix (SDK-603, PR #4997).
Makes pipeline startup recovery stop deleting completed work, and stamps each run's origin when it starts. A document is marked complete for a dataset the moment its own tasks finish, mid-run, and a later run skips documents already so marked — so when run A died with twelve documents done, run B processed the rest and skipped those twelve, leaving the dataset complete. Recovery then closed A at a later boot with a whole-run rollback, which deleted those twelve documents' artifacts and cleared their marks, dropping the dataset to twenty-eight documents with nothing to refill it until someone ran cognify() again. Recovery now closes an abandoned run as ERRORED while keeping the documents it completed. Alongside it, the INITIATED reset row and the pipeline cache gate are gone, and a run's origin is stamped at start rather than inferred afterwards, so diagnostics attribute activity to the right run; on ingestion, a refresh lets the route stamp follow the content rather than staying pinned to the original upload path (COG-6606, SDK-587, PRs #5090, #5091, #5104, #5107, #5122).
Records the embedding model on each dataset and checks it once, so changing EMBEDDING_MODEL under an existing dataset fails with a clear EmbeddingDimensionMismatchError instead of silently degrading recall. A dataset's vectors are only comparable to a query embedded by the same model; swapping the model left the stored vectors in place and the mismatch surfaced only as steadily worse results. The model is recorded in the dataset's existing dataset_database row alongside the rest of its vector-store connection info, so there is no schema change and no migration — and the check sits in the dataset registry rather than in the vector adapters, which is what keeps it free on the happy path: an adapter-level check would have read the collection schema (LanceDB) or the pg_attribute catalog (pgvector) before every create_data_points and every search, four extra round trips per GRAPH_COMPLETION question on every deployment forever, to catch a state that exists only just after someone changes the setting (SDK-756, PR #5117).
Adds GET /api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/processing-status, which answers the question the existing dataset status endpoints could not: not whether a run is going or done, but which of a dataset's individual items carry the per-item completion stamp for a pipeline. The response is {total, completed, pending, items}, where items is {id, name, completed}] with one entry per data item in the same order as GET /api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/data, and each id is the data_id accepted by DELETE /api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/data/{data_id} and forget(data_id=...) — so a pending item can be acted on straight from the response. The optional pipeline query parameter picks which pipeline's stamp is counted, defaulting to cognify_pipeline (add_pipeline and code_graph_pipeline are the other pipeline names Cognee stamps items with; an unknown name is not rejected and simply reports every item as pending). Authorization and error codes match the other per-dataset routes such as GET /api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/data: read on the dataset is required, a missing or unreadable dataset is a 404, and a failure to compute the status is a 409. One semantic to hold onto when building on it: per-item errored state is not persisted, so pending lumps together untouched, in-flight, and failed items, and a row whose pipeline_status is NULL counts as pending — this is the distinction from /status/progress, whose run-level {completed_items, total_items, current_stage} counts an errored item as finished. Internally the completion check is now a shared predicate that recognises both stamp representations — the bare string that is written today and a dict form carrying the status under a "status" key, reserved for the planned hash-aware rollout so stamps can grow fields such as content_hash without breaking readers; nothing writes the dict form yet — and the incremental skip check tolerates a NULL pipeline_status. Additive and backward-compatible: no existing endpoint changes shape, no SDK method ships for it, and there is no configuration option, environment variable, or migration (SDK-23, PR #4971).
Fixes a cross-tenant leak in GET /api/v1/permissions/tenants/{tenant_id}/roles/users/{user_id}, where a manager authorized for one tenant could read a user's roles in another. get_user_roles selected roles by joining on the user id alone, ignoring tenant_id entirely, so the response carried every role the target held across all tenants — and answered for a user who had nothing to do with the tenant in the path. It now first checks for a UserTenant membership row for (user_id, tenant_id) and raises UserNotFoundError ("User not found in tenant.") when there is none, then filters the role query with Role.tenant_id == tenant_id. Client impact: a target user who does not exist or is not a member of the tenant in the path now returns 404 where the endpoint previously returned 200 with a list (empty for a nonexistent user, that user's own roles for an out-of-tenant one), and for a user who belongs to several tenants the list is narrower — only the roles of the tenant in the path. A member who holds no role in that tenant still receives an empty list, so empty now unambiguously means "a member with no roles" while 404 means "not a member"; clients that treated an empty list as "unknown user" need to branch on the status instead. The 403 for a caller without user-management permission in the tenant is unchanged, and it is still checked before the lookup, so an unauthorized caller cannot use the new 404 to probe for membership. No new endpoint, request or response field, permission type, environment variable, or migration ships with this change; see [Role Visibility (SDK-638, PR #5035).
Adds folder presort, an opt-in pre-ingestion pass that inspects a messy folder before anything is ingested, and the JSON graph-model DSL it is built on. Presort runs in two connected phases through remember(): remember(folder, dry_run="presort") scans the folder — never writing to it — and returns a PresortReport carrying junk files, exact-duplicate clusters, version candidates (report_v2.pdf), potential personal data, each file's already-in-cognee status, and a set of proposed dataset groupings; passing that report back as remember(report) ingests each selected group into its proposed dataset through the normal add → cognify chain with incremental_loading=True and the node set "presort", ""], returning {dataset_name: RememberResult}. auto_apply=True does both in one call. The analyze phase is deterministic — no LLM or embedding configuration is needed, and use_llm=True opts into content classification, deeper PII detection, and semantic grouping; without a configured LLM the apply phase degrades to staging files with add() rather than failing. The CLI gains --presort, --from-report, --apply, --apply-graph, and --allow-root alongside tuning flags (see the [CLI overview). Nothing changes unless you ask for it: dry_run widens to Unionbool, Literal["presort"]] and data accepts a report, both additive, and automatic presort of a plain remember(folder) happens only when [PRESORT_FOLDERS_ENABLED=true — even then only for a local directory targeting main_dataset with no session, dataset id, or content_type. Presort is the one path that does not inherit the permissive local-path default: with COGNEE_ALLOWED_LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS unset it falls back to a bounded root set rather than "anywhere", scanning is read-only, and personal-data samples are stored redacted — see Presort scan roots. The same PR adds graph_model_from_spec() and graph_spec_to_json_schema() to cognee.low_level, which compile a plain-JSON graph schema spec into the DataPoint-derived class you pass as graph_model — the same document the Cognee UI's graph-model editor produces (COG-6281, PR #4630).
Fixes neighborhood expansion ranking nodes it discovered as if they were irrelevant. When graph completion projects a memory fragment with neighborhood_depth, the nodes reached by graph traversal have no vector score of their own; the code meant to fill that in passed their ids through node_name, which filters node-set membership rather than node ids, so the lookup matched nothing and every expanded node kept a default distance penalty into triplet scoring. Expansion ids are now scored through a new optional score_by_ids adapter method that filters on row id and returns cosine distances in batches of at most 1,000 unique ids, without loading payloads or searching the whole collection — LanceDB (including its subprocess mode), PGVector, and Turso implement it, and LanceDB bypasses its approximate vector index so a requested node far from the query is still scored. Which adapter you run decides what you get: on those three, the same query with neighborhood_depth can now return different, better-ranked triplets; on any other vector adapter the previous penalty behavior stands unchanged. The fix covers single-query retrieval, where both the query vector and the seed ids are available — batch queries are unaffected. No public API signature, configuration option, environment variable, or migration ships with it; score_by_ids is optional, and a community adapter that does not implement it keeps working (PR #5038).
Fixes update() dropping a document's node sets from the chunks it rewrites, so a search scoped with node_name silently stopped matching content that had been updated. On the incremental path, both rehydrated and freshly written chunks now carry the document's belongs_to_set and source_node_set into graph and vector storage, matching what the cognify pipeline already does on full ingestion. No API signature, configuration option, or migration ships with the fix. Chunks written by an earlier update() are not repaired automatically; the fix stops future updates from dropping the tags (SDK-575, PR #4949).
Gives update() one result shape on every path, makes every full rebuild say why it ran, and stops a rebuild from losing the document. Previously the chunk-level path returned a summary dict while a full rebuild returned cognify's {dataset_id: PipelineRunInfo} mapping — which carried no document id and no reason, so nothing could be built on it. Every path now returns a dict validated by UpdateResult (cognee/api/v1/update/result.py), identical for local calls, PATCH /api/v1/update and serve(). The chunk-level summary is a strict superset of what shipped in 1.5.4 — result"status"] == "incremental" and result["kept_chunks"] keep working — with status gaining full_rebuild and failed, a new total_chunks (the count after the update, so "kept 29 of 30" reads off directly), data_id/dataset_id, duration_seconds, pipeline_run_id, and error: {error_class, message}. Every rebuild now carries fallback: {reason, detail}, drawn from a nine-value RefusalReason enum exposed in OpenAPI: the six engine-level causes (unsupported_backend, unsupported_chunker, unsupported_metadata, no_baseline, chunks_not_tiling, unreadable_text) plus three update() decides before consulting the engine (disabled, custom_extraction_config, per_call_db_config). A failed rebuild keeps its 500 status but sends this same body, so a client reads the error from the fields it reads counters from. The rebuild no longer deletes the document: it drops the memory with forget(memory_only=True) and lets a pinned re-add refresh the row in place, so a re-add that fails mid-rebuild leaves the row, its content and its files intact for the next cognify() — where the old delete-then-re-add sequence could leave no document at all. Separately, [add() now raises DocumentUpdateRequiredError (HTTP 409) pointing at cognee.update() when a file is re-added with new content, instead of silently creating a duplicate. Upgrade action: callers that inspected the full-rebuild mapping for PipelineRunErrored should read status == "failed" and error instead; callers that re-added changed files through add() must switch to update() (SDK-587, PR #5017).
Attaches the built distributions and their attestation to each GitHub release, so a wheel can be verified from the release page without querying GitHub's attestation store. Alongside cognee--py3-none-any.whl and cognee-.tar.gz, the release now carries cognee-.sigstore.json (the Sigstore bundle, usable with gh attestation verify --bundle) and cognee-.intoto.jsonl (the DSSE envelope, the shape the SLSA ecosystem expects). The provenance itself is not new — it already existed as PEP 740 attestations on PyPI and SLSA build provenance in GitHub's attestation store — it simply was not visible on the release page. The nightly PyPI canaries create no GitHub release and are unaffected; .devN pre-releases cut from dev get the assets too (SDK-570, PR #4936).
Fixes the default Ladybug/Kuzu graph store fabricating self-loop edges for a graph that has nodes but no relationships, which let a dataset with entities and no links answer graph completion queries from triplets that are not in your data. get_graph_data() returns a (nodes, edges) pair, and when its edge query came back empty while nodes existed, the Ladybug adapter filled the gap by synthesizing one (node_id, node_id, "SELF", {...}) tuple per node before returning — an artifact no other in-tree graph backend produces; Neo4j, Turso, Neptune, and the Postgres demo adapter all return an empty edge list in that case. The trigger was narrow: the fabrication fired only when every edge was missing, so a graph carrying at least one real relationship was never affected, and the (source_id, target_id, relationship_name, properties) edge contract is unchanged. The fix has two halves. The fabrication is removed, so an edge-less graph reports zero edges on every backend and everything reading the graph through get_graph_data() stops seeing the phantom self-loops — including retrieval, the edge vector index, visualization, report() and validate(), none of which filtered them out, alongside graph export and the migration paths, which did. Second, emptiness is now decided by nodes instead of edges: a graph or node set holding nodes and no relationships used to raise EntityNotFoundError (Empty graph projected from the database, Nodeset does not exist, or empty nodeset projected from the database) on every backend, and now projects with an empty edge list, so searching a freshly ingested dataset whose extraction produced entities but no links stops erroring out. Self-loops already written into an edge index, an export, or a migrated graph are not repaired automatically — the fix stops new ones from being produced, which is why the defensive filters on the export and migration paths stay; audit downstream tooling that counted SELF edges, deduplicated against them, or treated them as real relationships. No public API signature, configuration option, environment variable, or migration ships with the fix (issue #5042, PR #5047, carrying community fix #5043 by @ptimizeroracle, credited in PR #5087).
Surfaces the vector relevance number on CHUNKS and SUMMARIES results, so callers can rank or fuse results across retrievers instead of trusting return order. ChunksRetriever and SummariesRetriever now attach each hit's vector-search score to the payload they return, which lands on score and on raw"score"] alongside the original payload fields. The value is the raw backend distance (cosine distance for the built-in adapters), so a lower number is a better match; the recall reference spells out the caveats and which search types leave it None. A ScoredResult with a None payload now yields {"score": …} rather than raising TypeError. This is additive: existing keys are untouched and no configuration option or migration ships with it (COG-6309, PR #4931).
Adds the [Organizing Your Data demo, which ingests one mixed corpus — two sales-call transcripts, an API reference, and an architecture guide — three ways and asks the same questions under each layout, so the trade-offs are visible side by side. Everything in one dataset reproduces the complaint the demo exists to fix: the documented limit of 100 requests per minute and a rep's "unlimited requests" promise share one retrieval pool, and nothing in the query keeps the promise out of the answer. One dataset with node sets tags each item at write time (node_set="tech_docs", "acme_api"]) and scopes recall per query (node_name=["tech_docs"]) — the tags overlap on purpose, so a shared acme_api grouping cuts across the docs/calls split and a cross-domain question ("Where do our sales promises contradict the technical documentation?") is still answerable by simply not filtering. Separate [datasets put a hard boundary between tech and sales — own permissions, isolated storage, independent forget — with node sets still slicing per account inside each; the demo also flags the footgun that a recall() with no datasets argument spans every dataset you can read, so separating data at write time is not enough. The rule of thumb it teaches: node sets are tags, datasets are walls — start with node sets, move domains into separate datasets when they must never contaminate each other. The demo lives under examples/demos/organizing_your_data/ and is run directly from a source checkout; no public API signature, configuration option, environment variable, or migration ships with it, and no installed behavior changes (RES-36, PR #4980).
Removes the unused Graphiti wrapper and the graphiti install extra. cognee/tasks/temporal_awareness/ — build_graph_with_temporal_awareness(), search_graph_with_temporal_awareness(), and index_and_transform_graphiti_nodes_and_edges() — wrapped graphiti-core to build an episode-based temporal graph directly in Neo4j. Nothing in the codebase imported it and it forced a Neo4j-only dependency, so the second temporal path is gone and the native temporal pipeline is the supported one: pass temporal_cognify=True to remember() and query with SearchType.TEMPORAL, which works with any supported graph store rather than requiring Neo4j — see Time Awareness. Breaking for anyone who installed the extra or imported those helpers: cogneegraphiti] no longer resolves and graphiti-core is dropped from the lockfile, so remove the extra from your install command; the removed functions have no drop-in replacement, and an episode graph already built in Neo4j stays where it is, readable with Graphiti's own tooling but no longer reachable through Cognee. Unaffected: GraphitiSource, the COGX importer for Graphiti and Zep JSON exports, is untouched — it reads an exported JSON file and never depended on graphiti-core (see [Migrate Memory Systems with COGX). Two earlier entries below describe indexing fixes to index_and_transform_graphiti_nodes_and_edges() and the GraphitiNode copy loop; they stand as history, and the re-index they recommend is no longer possible from Cognee. No configuration option, environment variable, or migration ships with the removal (SDK-543, PR #4886).
Removes the Postgres hybrid adapter, which had already been unreachable. PostgresHybridAdapter moves out of tree to topoteretes/cognee-internal-plugins; its only entry point was USE_UNIFIED_PROVIDER=pghybrid, and every construction site for that — in get_unified_engine, get_graph_engine and create_vector_engine — had already been commented out, so setting the flag raised Unsupported hybrid provider: pghybrid rather than building an adapter. pghybrid is gone from UNIFIED_PROVIDERS along with the dead construction blocks and the three tests that exercised only it. No configuration that worked before stops working, since none could have (SDK-742, PR #5097).
Points the API reference playground at a reachable base URL. The published OpenAPI spec's first server entry was the static host https://api.cognee.ai, which does not resolve — it fails the TLS handshake — so a curl sample copied out of the reference, or a request fired from the "Try it" button, died at the connection before it ever reached Cognee. The entry is now the templated per-tenant pod https://{tenant}.aws.cognee.ai, carrying a tenant server variable that defaults to your-tenant, described as "Cognee Cloud: your tenant pod, named in the platform.cognee.ai dashboard"; the second entry, http://localhost:8000, is now described as "Self-hosted: a locally running cognee server". What readers do differently: the playground now exposes a Server section with a tenant field, prefilled your-tenant, and generated cURL samples substitute that default — so replace it with the tenant shown on your API Keys page before sending a request, since your-tenant is a placeholder and not a live host. The base-URL dropdown still offers http://localhost:8000 as the second server for a self-hosted instance. This changes the servers block of the published spec and nothing else: no runtime product behavior changes, and no public API signature, endpoint, configuration option, environment variable, or migration ships with it (RES-44, PR #5020).
Makes forget() fail with a typed error when a dataset name cannot be resolved, instead of crashing. forget(dataset="does-not-exist") — and any name you lack the delete permission on — used to raise AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'id' from dataset resolution; it now raises DatasetNotFoundError: Dataset '' not found or not accessible., worded identically for a missing and an unauthorized dataset so names are not leaked. Over HTTP, POST /api/v1/forget also stopped flattening typed errors into 500 {"error": "An error occurred during deletion."}: the router re-raises CogneeApiError subclasses so each renders its own status — 404 for the unknown name, 403 for a dataset_id you cannot delete (which already raised PermissionDeniedError on the SDK, but surfaced as a 500 over HTTP). The fix lands at the lookup site, so no surface shows the NoneType traceback any more — but only the SDK raises the typed DatasetNotFoundError and only HTTP renders the 404: the CLI still exits 1 with Failed to forget: ... and MCP still answers Error: Forget failed: ..., each now carrying the readable message. Update error handling if you matched on the AttributeError or on the generic 500. Parameter-validation behavior is unchanged — an invalid combination still raises ValueError and returns 422 — and no API signature, configuration option, environment variable, or migration ships with the fix (fixes #5013, PR #5032).
Fixes a stray f in the error message raised by get_dataset_ids(). A literal f sat just before the {datasets} placeholder in the f-string, so it was printed as part of the message and the DatasetTypeError read One or more of the provided dataset types is not handled: f'my_dataset', UUID('…')]. It now reads … is not handled: ['my_dataset', UUID('…')]. That is the error raised when the datasets list is neither all names nor all UUIDs — a mixed list, or an element of some other type — so it reaches callers through get_authorized_existing_datasets() and, over HTTP, as a 400 Bad Request. Message text only: the exception type, its name, its status code, and the condition that raises it are unchanged, as is the get_dataset_ids(datasets, user) signature. No public API signature, configuration option, environment variable, or migration ships with the fix (PR #4945).
Fixes a proxy spend cap escaping five [LLM adapters as a raw InstructorRetryException instead of the typed LLMPaymentRequiredError (HTTP 402).
